messages:
sachin: Seeing intermittent OOMs on meridian14b-int4 canary during spike tests. Happens when we ramp 180-220 rps. Pattern looks like big allocs tied to generation.max_new_tokens + KV prefetch, then fragmentation after warmstart.

anya: Which environment? dedicated or hosted canary?

sachin: Hosted canary (us-west-2), dedicated-small flavor. Minimal log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-18T14:03:21Z] alloc spike: +3.2GB on request id=0x7f9a2a
[2026-03-18T14:03:21Z] OOM: failed to reserve 1.1GB, free=200MB, frag_slots=12
[2026-03-18T14:03:22Z] kv-prefetch: reserved 512MB per-stream
```

jon: Sounds familiar — when default max_new_tokens is high and prefetch is on we see the runtime reserve headroom for both kv + output buffer, which pushes fragmented heaps into OOM on small instances. We had a similar flare on a different model.

maria: Quick mitigation to try in canary: lower generation default + turn off aggressive prefetch and add a mild slow-start. Example config to roll: 
```json
{
  "generation.max_new_tokens": "32",
  "runtime.kv.prefetch": "false",
  "batch.target_tokens": "1024",
  "batch.max_batch_size": "8",
  "runtime.eviction_policy": "frag-shrink",
  "eviction.frag_threshold_percent": "20",
  "serve.slow_start_seconds": "60"
}
```

sachin: I'll push config-v12 with those changes and start a 10% canary. Also adding a background heap-defrag cron at 5m intervals for the canary pool.

ci-bot: canary deploy started: meridian14b-int4 @ config-v12 by sachin — rolling 0->10% in us-west-2

maria: :thumbsup: If fragmentation still trends >20% run heap-shrink tool: `/tools/heap-shrink --pattern=kv --target=10% --dryrun=false`

jon: Also capture a perf trace for 256/512 token evals (alloc curve) so we can tune batch.target_tokens properly. Use `perf/alloc-trace --out s3://redwood-debug/meridian14b/alloc-3625.log`.

sachin: Will do. Tagging @eng-ml for visibility.

sachin: quick update after 10m: canary at 10% for 10m, no OOMs observed, latency +2ms p50 on gen path, resource usage smoothed. Keeping canary at 25% for 1h to validate.

maria: Nice. If stable, we can make generation.max_new_tokens=32 the per-model default for meridian14b-int4 until we validate quant-int8 behavior.

jon: One more note — add a regression eval to CI that runs a 1000-sample prompt set with max_new_tokens=48 to ensure quality doesn't degrade with the lower default.

sachin: Ack, will add eval job `regress/meridian14b/maxnew-48` to the pipeline.
